templates/method-statement.what_is_it:
A method statement is a document that describes how a particular task or activity will be carried out safely on a construction site. It details the step-by-step procedures, the hazards involved, the control measures in place, and the resources required.

CDM 2015 and the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 require you to assess risks and plan a safe system of work. A method statement is the usual way to set that out for higher-risk tasks, and principal contractors often require one before work starts.

It is sometimes called a safe system of work. Safe Work Method Statement (SWMS) is the Australian term; in the UK a method statement and its risk assessment together are usually called a RAMS.
templates/method-statement.when_to_use:
You need a method statement when:

- Starting any higher-risk construction activity (working at height, hot works, confined spaces, demolition, excavation, lifting operations, work near live services)
- The principal contractor or client requires one as part of their site rules
- A new subcontractor is mobilising to site
- The scope, sequence, plant or site conditions change from what was planned
- Following an incident or near miss where the existing method statement needs revision

Method statements should be prepared BEFORE work begins and briefed to all operatives who will carry out the work. They are living documents and should be updated whenever conditions change.
